name: Andorhal
region: Lordaeron, a shallow valley below a low rise on the south road; the King's road enters by a larger gate to the right

sensoryProfile.sight: Fills the shallow valley from side to side: a long low grey wall, roofs packed close behind it, chimney smoke from all of them. Above the roofs stand the granaries: tall square timber buildings on stone feet, each with a hoist beam jutting under the gable; on the nearest a sack goes up on its rope while a man leans from the loft door to take it. More beyond, a whole quarter of them. Grain dust lies over that quarter in a haze, the low sun turning it gold. Wagons stand in lines on the roads in; the line on this road runs down to the smaller gate; a longer line on a broad straight road to the right runs to a bigger gate. (Chapter 7, ground level at dusk: cobbles pale with spilled grain, every crack packed full; dust thick at the edges of the cobbles that shows every print; blind loading lanes; lamplit loft windows; new-lit lamps on bracket and gatepost; a pigeon on a ridge; dye cloth on tenter frames, blue and rust-red, slack in still air.)
sensoryProfile.sound: Iron tyres on cobbles, a bell, a dog that will not stop, a mill wheel, and under the dog a man singing a half-known rude song, badly. (Chapter 7: somebody hammering at a hoop; axles grinding loud enough to cover a troop of horse; the Exchange bell for the night shift, heavy and slow, answered by doors and wheels; a lamplighter whistling the same few notes; a woman singing a child the same flat line over and over.)
sensoryProfile.smell: Bake ovens in the warm air, through the dust. (Chapter 7: warm grain, dry and sweet, 'like bread before it goes in the oven', through the whole gate and through the shutters of the post; the sour stink of dye vats in Tenter Row; no wet streets.)
sensoryProfile.touch: Under all the noise the drag beats, slow and late, 'so much bigger than it had been all morning that she could feel it in the roots of her teeth'. (Chapter 7: warm still dusk; grit and soot on the roofs; Jaina's lip draws back in the arch's shade as if the air had an edge; frost on her linen on a warm night.)
sensoryProfile.atmosphere: Busy, ordinary, working: the horror is that it is alive. Not Millhaven. At ground level the city is more paper than weak points: tallies, bills, seals, books and bells; a place where an operation can sit inside ordinary labour.

establishedFacts.fact: Andorhal is a working walled city with a granary quarter of tall timber buildings on stone feet with hoist beams. Seen at the end of the afternoon (low sun). The party approaches by the back way (the south road), not the King's road front gate.
The gate on the south road is the market gate: a militia post sits just inside on the left, with a bench outside its door.
Local authority is split among factors, the corn guild and the town (per the tally-man), who 'will sit you on a bench in the hall till they light the lamps'.
The drag is far stronger here than anywhere on the road; Jaina feels it in her teeth. Every road she marked on Sylvanas's sheet comes in here.

The wall at the market gate is field stone no higher than a man's chest from the road, mortar crumbling and patched; there is no ward-stone in it anywhere. Every cart still has to stop under the arch for a clerk. Gate guards spike every sack ('Since the Exchange said'); the Exchange (the Corn Exchange, whose bell rings shifts) and a magistrate and town council run local authority.
The gate clerk's book and a man chalking each wagon turned toward the granary lane at the corner are two separate counts of who comes in.

Mill Lane runs from the weir bridge to the Corn Exchange; four yards on it (Holt's, Fenner's, the Exchange granary, Garside's) and the streets that buy bread off the bakers at the bottom. Behind them runs Hurdle Lane, with Tenter Row off it (dyers; Kett's at the bottom). The tavern for loaders is the Wheatsheaf. The weir and the weir road, the south road and the east road are the outbound grain routes.

The inspection offices and the mage quarter lie across the city from the post; a Kirin Tor house is there; the sample room opens only to a magister's ring; there is also a copy room. The inspection office keeps the second copy of every bill that leaves under a yard's mark.
The Exchange bell rings the shifts: day crews go off at the evening bell and night crews go in; it rings again for the day. Militia night men go out on the lanes at the bell.

Sickness cluster: Mill Lane since spring, bad from high summer; the old and babies first; the physicians call it 'the river damp'. A widow on one corner has lost both her lodgers while her sister across the way, who buys from a different oven, has not been ill.

eventsHere.event: First sight from the crest: Jaina sees a living city and understands that whoever keeps the spread running is inside. 'The market gate.'

Entry through the market gate on Sylvanas's Farstrider pass; militia post; Havel and Corin's two halves; the split (Jaina, Corin and Lyriel to the sample room; Sylvanas, Cyndia and Havel to the granary district); Sylvanas's tail of the runner to Kett's loft; the table at the post; the decision to take a living cultist that night.
